verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              सहदेवं तथा क्रुद्धं दहन्तं तव वाहिनीम् । दुःशासनो महाराज भ्राता भ्रातरमभ्ययात् ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said O great monarch, Dushasana rushed against Shahadeva, that is, brother against brother, who was highly enraged and blasted your army.

verses.sanskrit: तौ समेतौ महायुद्धे दृष्ट्वा तत्र महारथाः । सिंहनादरवांश्चक्रुर्वासांस्यादुधुवुश्च ह ॥२॥
verses.english: In the field of battle, the mighty carwarriors, seeing those two thus engaged in a encounter, began to uiter shouts resembling the roars of lions and to wave their cloths.

verses.sanskrit: ततो भारत क्रुद्धेन तव पुत्रेण धन्विना । पाण्डुपुत्रस्त्रिभिर्बाणैर्वक्षस्यभिहतो बली ॥३॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, the most powerful son of Pandu was decply struck in the chest with three shafts by the bowman, your son, who was highly enraged.

verses.sanskrit: सहदेवस्ततो राजन्नाराचेन तवात्मजम् । विद्ध्वा विव्याध सप्तत्या सारथिं च त्रिभिः शरैः ॥४॥
verses.english: Then, O monarch, Shahadeva, after having first pierced your son, again struck him with seventy shafts, as well as his charioteer with threc others.

verses.sanskrit: दुःशासनस्ततश्चापं छित्त्वा राजन्महाहवे । सहदेवं त्रिसप्तत्या बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत् ॥५॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O king, Dushasana, after having severed his bow in that dreadful battle, struck Shahadeva with seventy-three arrows both in the arms and the chest.

verses.sanskrit: सहदेवस्तु संक्रुद्धः खड्गं गृह्य महाहवे । आविध्य प्रासृजत्तूर्णं तव पुत्ररथं प्रति ॥६॥
verses.english: Then the highly enraged Shahadeva, after having taken up his sword and turned it round, had hurled it immediately towards the ear of your son in that fierce encounter.

verses.sanskrit: समार्गणगुणं चापं छित्त्वा तस्य महानसिः । निपपात ततो भूमौ च्युतः सर्प इवाम्बरात् ॥७॥
verses.english: Thus having severed his (Dusasana's) bow along with its string and arrow, then that fearful sword fell down upon the earth, even as a snake falls down from heaven upon the ground.

verses.sanskrit: अथान्यद्धनुरादाय सहदेवः प्रतापवान् । दुःशासनाय चिक्षेप बाणमन्तकरं ततः ॥८॥
verses.english: Thereupon Shahadeva, possessed of immerise prowess, having taken up another bow, hurled at Dushasana a shaft, capable of bringing about death.

verses.sanskrit: तमापतन्तं विशिखं यमदण्डोपमत्विषम् । खड्गेन शितधारेण द्विधा चिच्छेद कौरवः ॥९॥
verses.english: Then the son of Kuru had severed into two fragments, with his keen-edged sword, that shaft, which was as resplendent as the very rod of Death himself, directed towards him.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तं निशितं खड्गमाविध्य युधि सत्वरः । धनुश्चान्यत्समादाय शरं जग्राह वीर्यवान् ॥१०॥
verses.english: Then having turned round that sharp-edged sword in the field of battle, the most powerful one took up another bow most rapidly and grasped an arrow.

verses.sanskrit: तमापतन्तं सहसा निस्त्रिंशं निशितैः शरैः । पातयामास समरे सहदेवो हसन्निव ॥११॥
ततो बाणांश्चतुःषष्टिं तव पुत्रो महारणे । सहदेवरथं तूर्णं प्रेषयामास भारत ॥१२॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, your son most rapidly directed sixty-four arrows against the car of Shahadeva, in that dreadful battle.

verses.sanskrit: ताञ्छरान्समरे राजन् वेगेनापततो बहून् । एकैकं पञ्चभिर्बाणैः सहदेवो न्यकृन्तत ॥१३॥
verses.english: Then Shahadeva, O monarch, cut-off every one of these innumerable arrows, that were falling with speed (upon him) with five shafts of his own in that battle.

verses.sanskrit: सन्निवार्य महाबाणांस्तव पुत्रेण प्रेषितान् । अथास्मै सुबहून्बाणान्प्रेषयामास संयुगे ॥१४॥
verses.english: Having thus restrained those powerful arrows, shot by your son, he (Shahadeva) sent away innumerable shafts against him (his antagonist) in that dreadful battle.

verses.sanskrit: तान्बाणांस्तव पुत्रोऽपि छित्त्वेकैकं त्रिभिः शरैः । ननाद सुमहानादं दारयाणो वसुन्धराम् ॥१५॥
verses.english: Your son, too, having severed every one of these arrows with three shafts of his own, sent out a great uproar; and thereby caused the whole earth echo with it.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दुःशासनो राजन् विद्ध्वा पाण्डुसुतं रणे । सारथिं नवभिर्बाणैर्माद्रेयस्य समार्पयत् ॥१६॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O monarch, Dushasana, having pierced the son of Pandu in that battle, had struck the charioteer of the Madraya chief with nine shafts.

verses.sanskrit: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज सहदेवः प्रतापवान् । समाधत्त शरं घोरं मृत्युकालान्तकोपमम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: O mighty monarch, the most powerful Shahadeva, being highly enraged at this, fixed an arrow on his bow, that was as deadly as Death himself.

verses.sanskrit: विकृष्य बलवच्चापं तव पुत्राय सोऽसृजत् । स तं निर्भिद्य वेगेन भित्त्वा च कवचं महत् ॥१८॥
verses.english: Then having stretched his bow with great force, he shot that arrow at your son. O monarch, that shaft, after having successively pierced with great force through his body and his strong armour, itself entered into the earth, even as the snakes enter into the ant-hill. Thereupon, O king, your son, that mighty carwarrior, became senseless.

verses.sanskrit: प्राविशद्धरणीं राजन् वल्मीकमिव पन्नगः । ततः संमुमुहे राजंस्तव पुत्रो महारथः ॥१९॥
मूढं चैनं समालोक्य सारथिस्त्वरितो रथम् । अपोवाह भृशं त्रस्तो वध्यमानः शितैः शरैः ॥२०॥
verses.english: Having seen him thus senseless and himself being deeply struck with sharp arrows, his charioteer with great rapidity carried away the car.

verses.sanskrit: पराजित्य रणे तं तु कौरव्यं पाण्डुनन्दनः । दुर्योधनबलं दृष्ट्वा प्रममाथ समन्ततः ॥२१॥
verses.english: Having defeated that Kuru warrior in battle, the son of Pandu looked at the army of Duryodhana and crushed it on all sides.

verses.sanskrit: पिपीलिकपुटं राजन्यथा मृदूनन्नरो रुषा । तथा सा कौरवी सेना मृदिता तेन भारत ॥२२॥
verses.english: O descendant of the Bharata race, O monarch, that force belonging to the Kurus was crushed by the son of Pandu, even as a swarm of ants is crushed to death by a man with great rage.
